text.p: The power of world number one Pete Sampras defeated doubles specialist Todd Woodbridge on Friday, as the American ran away with their Wimbledon semifinal 6-2 6-1 7-6.
Sampras thumped down only 10 aces in the one hour 44-minute match, fewer than average, but Woodbridge still found his serve too big to return.
The slight Australian, at 1.78m, seven cm shorter than the three-times champion, was volleyed and smashed out of the match.
His service could not penetrate Sampras's defence and he was broken twice in the first two sets and once in the third.
He did hit back with some neat lobbing and passing to break Sampras back, but had no answer to Sampras's all-round speed and power in the tie-break, which he lost 7-3.
Sampras won with a huge serve that Woodbridge could not return.

Sampras now goes in search of a fourth Wimbledon crown against either Michael Stich of Germany or Cedric Pioline of France, while Woodbridge continues the defence of his doubles title with partner Mark Woodforde in the semifinals.
